posts.content_md:
3-D Holographic Spirographs (SpiroHoloGraphs)

Ok, this may be far out and I would love to try it but I am afraid I don’t have the necessary equipment. I may give the first part a try by hand though.

First take a film plate and lay it on the table with a front surface mirror under it.. Then take a Spirograph outer ring and fasten it to a piece of glass. Mount this just over the plate and mirror. Use a piece of opaque material to block all but inside the ring. Also blacken the ring itself so that it is also opaque. Now, take the inner disk and cover it with a large piece of rigid black material such that no matter what position it is in within the outer ring all of the rest of the inner hole of the outer ring is covered. Now make a hole in the opaque material where you want to insert the laser “pen”. The disk’s original hole may need to be enlarged. Glue a small bearing so that is it centered over the hole. Now attach a handle to the outside of the race bearing. This allows you to move the inner disk around the Spirograph as normal. Enlarge a beam to cover then entire area of the inside of the inner ring. As the beam is stable and remains in position and only the hole is being moved the system should produce interference patterns where the hole is. Speed would have to be controlled.

Now for truly 3D, mount the film plate about 3 inches above the table. Take the front surface mirror and replace it with a white card. Have this white card on a translation table that moves in the Y axis (up and down) direction. While the wheel is being turned the Y axis can be moved either up or down to produce truly 3D effects. If it is possible to automate the wheel movement and the up down movement, a very volumized Spirographic sphere could be made.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I was thinking more on this and relize the object card cannot be moving during the exposure or the phase information would be lost.

WHat could be done is a white card can be place at an angle to the plate behind it. Then the SpiroHologram can be done. It would look like a flat pattern with part of it close to the plate and the other end further from the plate. Then a second SpiroHoloGram could be made with the white card at a different angle. Thus the two flat SpiroHolograms would be in different planes and bisect or intersect one another. Possible more then two could be done.

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md: How about this suggestion: Make the spirograph pattern on film or glass without recording the hologram (a heck of a lot easier!) and then use that as a stencil for recording the hologram in the manner you had described without moving the contraption.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Ed that would be a lot easier and might be fun to do as a first step. Not being able to move the background reflector in sync with the circular movement of the Spirograph does take away the truly 3D I was looking for. 

I am having a problem drawing and visualizing the effect if the card was slanted. Then it seems that the only hologram one point on the card would make would be at exactly one reference point on the emulsion. This may lead to a very narrow or even a single viewing angle for points far away from the plate, thus limiting depth.

I guess what I am looking for is a way to draw 3D lines and patterns in air behind a reflection hologram. Kind of like a spherical pattern of lines something like what is produced in a Spirograph, with the possibility of having more then one intersect, bisect or be a subset of others and the possibility of altering the sphere into egg shapes etc….

I was thinking in DCG if the speed of the movement was also varied, thus the energy that part of the plate got, then the colors would come out different. 

Unless of course a pulsed laser is used in conjunction with stepper motors and translation stages to do all the choreographed movements, then that would be cool. Now that I think about it, that little pulsed laser Bill Jensen is working on just might do the trick. But having a small reference spot being used only for a small object spot may present problems. Hummmm, got to think that one out. Maybe the reference spot and the reflecting object need to be kept stationary and the plate itself needs to be moved in all three axes.
